statements.impact_statement: RASC is not in the explicit decoder allowlist; only h264, prores, mpeg4 and mjpeg video decoders are accepted.
The VobSub .sub/.idx demuxer is outside the mov format allowlist; subtitle codecs are not in the decoder allowlist.
The Debian FFmpeg build does not enable CUDA/NVDEC. CI asserts that CUDA hardware acceleration and *_cuvid/NVDEC decoders are absent.
The render command always muxes MP4 output with H.264/AAC; it never selects the S/PDIF muxer.
RTP/ASF demuxing is not allowed: input protocols are restricted to file,pipe and demuxers to mov.
ADX/AAX codecs are not in the explicit decoder allowlist; the accepted audio codecs are AAC, MP3, PCM, ALAC, AC3, EAC3 and FLAC.
The renderer constructs a fixed filter graph (trim, setpts, fps, scale, pad, setsar, format, overlay, amix); hqdn3d is not reachable and custom filters are rejected.
CAF is outside the mov demuxer allowlist and MACE6 is not in the decoder allowlist.
The renderer outputs only H.264/AAC MP4 and does not invoke PNG/APNG encoders; PNG input is also excluded by the codec allowlist.
PGS/SUP subtitle input is outside the supported demuxer/codec allowlists; the renderer maps only video and optional audio streams.
WTV is outside the mov demuxer allowlist and DVB subtitle codecs are not accepted.
CFHD is not in the explicit video decoder allowlist; the format and codec allowlists reject this path before decode.
HEVC is excluded from the input codec allowlist; the renderer always decodes and re-encodes accepted video with libx264.
The output container is MP4 only; the MPEG-PS muxer is never selected.
The RIST protocol is excluded by the file,pipe protocol whitelist; uploaded media is read from local temporary files only.
The renderer does not use RTP output or the VC-2/Dirac RTP packetizer; it always writes MP4.
DASH is excluded by the mov demuxer allowlist and network protocols are not permitted.
The Debian FFmpeg build does not enable mbedTLS, and source-media processing permits only file,pipe protocols. The vulnerable tls_mbedtls transport is not compiled or reachable.
SFTP is not in the file,pipe protocol allowlist; uploaded assets are local files and the worker never opens SFTP URLs.
DASH is not in the mov demuxer allowlist; the worker does not open manifests or network streams.
HLS is not in the mov demuxer allowlist; playlist inputs are rejected before demuxing.
RTSP is not in the file,pipe protocol allowlist; the worker processes only local temporary files.
HLS is not in the mov demuxer allowlist; HLS child-playlist handling is not reachable.
The IMF demuxer is not in the mov format allowlist.
Go2Meeting G2M decoders are not in the explicit codec allowlist.
PCX is not in the explicit codec allowlist; uploaded image assets are not accepted as source media.
Sun Raster is not in the explicit codec allowlist; uploaded image assets are not accepted as source media.
CDXL is not in the explicit codec allowlist; uploaded image assets are not accepted as source media.
Huffyuv is not in the explicit codec allowlist; only the listed video codecs can be decoded.
TDSC is not in the explicit codec allowlist; only the listed video codecs can be decoded.

Debian classifies this as an unimportant issue with no security impact; the advisory describes a memory leak in a CLI path, not an exploitable confidentiality, integrity, or availability issue in this service.
The vulnerable target_sws_fuzzer() is a fuzz-test target, not code included or invoked by the production FFmpeg CLI/runtime.
TDSC is not in the explicit codec allowlist; only the listed video codecs can be decoded.
The ffconcat demuxer is not in the mov allowlist and the renderer never supplies -safe 0 or concat manifests.
The vf_floodfill filter is not in the renderer's fixed filter graph; caller-supplied filters are rejected.
The vf_swaprect filter is not in the renderer's fixed filter graph; caller-supplied filters are rejected.
IAMF is not in the mov demuxer allowlist.
The LCL/ZLIB video decoder is not in the explicit codec allowlist.
RSCC is not in the explicit codec allowlist.
Screenpresso is not in the explicit codec allowlist.
TIFF is not in the explicit codec allowlist; standalone image inputs are not accepted as source media.
HLS is not in the mov demuxer allowlist; the worker does not process HLS playlists.

All uploaded-source ffprobe and FFmpeg inputs are constrained by the shared input policy: only the MOV demuxer and H.264, ProRes, MPEG-4 Part 2, and MJPEG video codecs are allowed. Matroska/WebM, HEVC, and AV1 are excluded; the OpenCV/PySceneDetect reader was removed, so no alternate media parser bypasses the allowlist. The reported T.35 BlockAdditional and HEVC/AV1 SEI trigger paths are therefore outside the supported input surface. This is an application-level reachability determination, not a patched FFmpeg package.

Before ffprobe runs, the worker parses ISO-BMFF atom headers and rejects PSSH atoms. Every FFmpeg source input also passes through media_input_args(), which performs the same rejection before adding -i. The parser covers top-level atoms and direct moov/moof children, handles 32-bit, extended-size, and size-to-end headers, and fails closed on malformed tables or excessive atom counts. Regression tests cover top-level and moov PSSH atoms, extended-size PSSH, malformed atom sizes, and the render input boundary. DRM-protected inputs are not supported. This is an application-level input exclusion, not a patched FFmpeg package.

The vulnerable code is in the infocmp command-line executable. The runtime image removes /usr/bin/infocmp and CI verifies that the executable is absent. The essential ncurses-bin package remains installed for other terminal utilities; the remaining ncurses runtime libraries and terminfo data do not provide the vulnerable infocmp program.

The vulnerable Archive::Tar module is not installed in either runtime image. CI verifies that Perl cannot load Archive::Tar; only the minimal perl-base runtime remains. The application does not parse untrusted tar archives through Perl.

The vulnerability is in the systemd-homed account-management daemon. Neither systemd-homed executable nor service is installed in the runtime images; EDITFLOW uses a static /etc/passwd account and does not configure the systemd NSS module. CI verifies the homed executables are absent.

The vulnerable libwebp encoder is never selected. The renderer maps only its generated video stream and optional audio stream, then explicitly encodes video with libx264 and audio with AAC; callers cannot choose output encoders or supply custom filter graphs.

The vulnerable DVD subtitle encoder is never selected. The renderer maps only its generated video stream and optional audio stream, explicitly encodes video with libx264 and audio with AAC, and does not map or encode subtitle streams.

HEVC/AV1 hardware and OBU paths are also excluded. A regression test asserts that the supported codec set remains exact.

This issue requires libxml2's Python bindings. The Worker SBOM contains the libxml2 shared library but no python3-libxml2 package, Python libxml2 module, or lxml component; the application requirements also contain no libxml2 Python binding. The vulnerable SAX binding callback is therefore not present in the deployed image.

The vulnerable V4L2 M2M output encoder is never selected. The renderer's output command explicitly selects the software libx264 encoder for video and AAC for audio; users cannot choose an output encoder or supply a custom output codec. A regression test asserts the render plan pins -c:v to libx264 and excludes v4l2m2m.

The vulnerable flow requires the privileged mount(8) executable to invoke an external mount helper and run libmount post-mount hooks. The Worker and API images delete the mount and umount executables after package installation; CI asserts that neither command is present in either final image. The application does not invoke mount operations.

The vulnerable --join-cgroup option is implemented by nsenter(8). The Worker and API images delete the nsenter executable after package installation; CI asserts that the command is absent from both final images. The application does not enter host namespaces or join cgroups.

The vulnerable X-mount.subdir path requires mount(8) to process an fstab mount entry. The Worker and API images delete the mount and umount executables after package installation; CI asserts that neither command is present in either final image. The application does not invoke mount operations.

The vulnerable restricted bind-mount path requires the privileged mount(8) executable to process an fstab entry with X-mount.owner/group/mode. The Worker and API images delete the mount and umount executables after package installation; CI asserts that neither command is present in either final image. The application does not invoke mount operations.

The affected code paths are Kerberos KDC/kadmind server operations (KDC ASN.1 request processing, KDB/KDC operations, or kadmind GSS-RPC administrative services). The Worker image contains only the client-side Kerberos shared libraries as transitive dependencies; it does not contain or run krb5kdc, kadmind, kadmin, kadmin.local, or kdb5_util. The application does not implement a Kerberos KDC or administrative service. FFmpeg source media is restricted to file and pipe protocols, so it cannot expose these server RPC endpoints. CI asserts the KDC/admin executables are absent and a regression test locks the media protocol allowlist to file,pipe. Reassess if Kerberos server packages or network media protocols are added.

The Worker SBOM shows libopenjp2-7 is consumed only by FFmpeg's libavcodec61. The vulnerable code paths are JPEG 2000/OpenJPEG decoding or conversion routines; the application's exact codec allowlist excludes jpeg2000 and the demuxer allowlist is MOV only. CI regression tests assert jpeg2000 is not an allowed decoder. No other installed component depends on this library in the generated Worker SBOM. Reassess if JPEG 2000 is enabled or another consumer is added.

The Worker SBOM dependency graph shows libxi6 is consumed only by libsdl2, which is used by FFmpeg's optional SDL output device. The application render plan never selects an SDL output device (it writes the fixed MP4 output with libx264); a regression test asserts that no -f output-device selector is present. CI additionally verifies that DISPLAY is unset, no X11 socket exists, and Xorg/Xvfb/Xwayland servers are absent. These CVEs require a malicious X server to send XInput replies to a connected client, and the Worker has no X server connection path. Reassess if SDL output or X11 support is added.
